summary.text: Norma Torres is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 35th District in the Inland Empire. Born in Guatemala, she worked as an LAPD 911 dispatcher before serving as Pomona mayor and in both houses of the California Legislature, and she has served in Congress since 2015. She sits on the Appropriations Committee and describes her focus as federal funding for the Inland Empire, public safety and Central America policy.

paragraphs.text: Immigrated to the United States from Guatemala; her official biography describes her as the only Central American-born Member of Congress and says she lives in Pomona with her husband and sons.

Worked as a 911 dispatcher with the Los Angeles Police Department for 17 years and was a member of AFSCME Local 3090; her official biography says she led efforts to improve 911 service in Los Angeles.
Earned a bachelor's degree in labor studies from the National Labor College (2012, per Ballotpedia).
Served on the Pomona, California City Council from 2000 to 2006 and as mayor of Pomona from 2006 to 2008.

Served in the California state Legislature from 2008 to 2014, first in the Assembly and then in the Senate; her official biography says that as a state senator she worked on implementation of the Affordable Care Act in California and authored legislation to modernize the 9-1-1 system.

Has served in the U.S. House since 2015 and, according to her official biography, is a senior member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development and chairs the Congressional Hispanic Caucus FAA Reauthorization Task Force; Ballotpedia lists her 2025-2026 assignments as Appropriations, House Administration and the Joint Committee on the Library.
Her official biography credits her with the Central American Women and Children Act and with passing the Enrique Roman-Martinez Military Cold Case Justice Act.
Volunteered with the American Youth Soccer Organization, Big Sisters Program, Boy Scouts and Suicide Prevention Center, according to Ballotpedia.
